opening.text: On a cold night, a blanket doesn't make the cold go away. But it holds the warmth in, and you can sleep. Grief is a cold night. Nothing we say will make it vanish. But God gives comfort that wraps around us and holds us until morning.

mainMessage.text: God's comfort is a blanket on a cold night. It doesn't end the grief. It helps us bear it.

blocks.text: **He knows our sorrow** The Savior isn't far from our pain. He has carried it.
Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “The Comforter” from the April 2015 general conference (General Women’s Session).
One of the attributes of the Savior we most appreciate is His infinite compassion.
He knows our sorrow.
**Comfort comes by the Spirit** The Savior promised that we would not be left alone. He sends the Comforter.
I will not leave you comfort-less: I will come to you.
Sister Reyna I. Aburto, Second Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency, said this in her talk “The Grave Has No Victory” from the April 2021 general conference.
That day I realized that the Spirit had given me comfort in a difficult time.
The Spirit comforts.
**Peace the world can't give** The world offers distractions. The Savior offers peace.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
Elder Matthew J. Eyring, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Comfort from the Holy Ghost” from the October 2026 general conference.
The Savior’s peace is made manifest through the comforting power of the Holy Ghost.
His peace is real.
**The grief stays, the strength grows** Comfort doesn't mean the sadness disappears. It means we are strengthened to carry it. Others can help us carry it too.

And it came to pass that he said unto them: Behold, here are the waters of Mormon (for thus were they called) and now, as ye are desirous to come into the fold of God, and to be called his people, and are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light;
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “The Comforter” from the April 2015 general conference (General Women’s Session).
The burden of grief did not disappear, but they were made able to bear the sorrow.
We can bear it.
**Death is not the end** The Resurrection changes how we face loss. Those we love still live.
Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
Sister Reyna I. Aburto, Second Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency, said this in her talk “The Grave Has No Victory” from the April 2021 general conference.
I had received a witness that my brother’s spirit is not dead; he is alive.
They live.
**Hope in Jesus Christ** Grief and hope can live in the same heart. Our hope is in Him.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
Elder Matthew J. Eyring, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Comfort from the Holy Ghost” from the October 2026 general conference.
There is hope in Jesus Christ.
Hope remains.

story.title: Jesus at the tomb of Lazarus

blocks.text: Lazarus was dead. His sisters were heartbroken. Jesus came to them.

Jesus wept. And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth. And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
Jesus wept with them first. Then He showed His power over death. Both are true of Him.

story.title: Mary at the empty tomb

blocks.text: Mary stood weeping at the tomb. She thought her Lord was gone.

Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away. Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.
Her grief was deep. And then He spoke her name. The one she mourned was alive. He knows our names too.

story.title: Elijah and the widow’s son

blocks.text: A widow had lost her son. Elijah had stayed in her home. He carried the boy up and prayed.

And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived. And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother: and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.
God heard a prayer in the dark. The mother received her son back. Heaven listens when we grieve.

story.title: The Savior who knows how to help

blocks.text: Alma taught his people what the Savior would do for them.

And he shall go forth, suffering pains and afflictions and temptations of every kind; and this that the word might be fulfilled which saith he will take upon him the pains and the sicknesses of his people. And he will take upon him death, that he may loose the bands of death which bind his people; and he will take upon him their infirmities, that his bowels may be filled with mercy, according to the flesh, that he may know according to the flesh how to succor his people according to their infirmities.
He took our pain on Himself so that He would know how to help. The companion beside us knows the road because He has walked it.
